section_title: Jesus Leads the Way to Jerusalem

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 32 As they were going up the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking ahead of them. The disciples were amazed, but those who followed were afraid. Again Jesus took the Twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him: 33 “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles, 34 who will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him. And after three days He will rise again.”

context_lines: Jesus walks ahead as the group travels toward Jerusalem. The disciples are amazed and those following are afraid. Mark reports their reactions without describing the exact thought behind each one. Jesus takes the Twelve aside and again explains what will happen to Him.

This announcement adds detail to those in [Mark 8:31](https://biblehub.com/bsb/mark/8.htm) and [9:30–32](https://biblehub.com/bsb/mark/9.htm). Jerusalem is named, as are condemnation by the chief priests and scribes, delivery to the Gentiles, mockery, spitting, flogging, killing, and resurrection after three days.

The prediction places humiliation and death alongside resurrection. Jesus is leading them toward a mission whose cost He knows. The request for positions of glory in the next scene will again show how hard the disciples find it to take in the path He describes.
common_interpretation_lines: Christian readings commonly understand this as Jesus deliberately preparing the disciples for His suffering and resurrection. [Wesley on Mark 10:32](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-gospel-according-to-st-mark/) emphasizes His courage in going forward and His care in telling them more fully what lies ahead.
god_plan_lines: After the resurrection, Jesus explains in [Luke 24:25–27](https://biblehub.com/bsb/luke/24.htm) that the Christ's suffering and entrance into glory belong to what the prophets announced. The detailed warning here is part of that larger purpose, even before the disciples can understand it.

The church's proclamation in [Acts 2:22–24](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/2.htm) holds together God's purpose, the responsibility of those who put Jesus to death, and God's raising Him. His announcement is not simply advance notice of tragedy. It prepares for the saving work that leads through death to resurrection and becomes the heart of the gospel.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
